essayIssues.opening_boilerplate: The opening uses application boilerplate. Consider replacing it with a concise, truthful moment or question relevant to this prompt.
essayIssues.long_first_sentence: The opening sentence is long. Consider splitting or shortening it while preserving its original meaning.
essayIssues.cliche_opening: The opening contains a common phrase. Replace it only with a specific experience that actually happened to you.
essayIssues.too_few_paragraphs: The draft has few paragraph breaks. Separate distinct ideas where the prompt and response length call for it.
essayIssues.paragraph_too_long: One paragraph is long. Consider splitting it where the subject or main idea changes.
essayIssues.no_conclusion: The ending may need a clearer close. Respond to the prompt without adding a new, unsupported claim.
essayIssues.run_on_sentences: Several sentences are long. Review sentence boundaries and vary length where that improves clarity.
essayIssues.no_evidence: This simple check did not detect a numeric detail. It may miss named evidence; clarify a real example and your role if relevant, without inventing numbers.
essayIssues.thin_evidence: The check detected few numeric details. Named examples may not be detected; add numbers only when you can verify them.
essayIssues.unsupported_adjective: A self-description phrase was detected. Consider showing the quality through an action you actually took rather than relying on the label alone.
essayIssues.cliches: Common application phrases were detected. Replace only those that do not express your specific experience.
essayIssues.passive_voice: Passive constructions were detected. Where accurate, state who performed the action; keep passive voice when the actor is unknown or less relevant.
essayIssues.monotone_rhythm: Sentence lengths are similar. Consider varying them where that would make the passage easier to follow.
essayIssues.repeated_word: A repeated word was detected. Review the quoted passage for an accidental duplicate.
essayIssues.target_not_named: The supplied target name was not detected as a whole word. Check whether this prompt asks you to name the university or programme.
essayIssues.why_us_generic: The check did not detect a specific programme feature. Add one only if it answers the prompt and you have verified it on an official source.
essayIssues.over_limit: The draft has {words} words, above the entered limit of {limit}. Trim it to meet the prompt's stated limit.
essayIssues.under_limit: The draft has {words} of {limit} words (under 60% of the limit). Check whether the prompt asks for more before adding text.
essayIssues.no_forward_look: A future goal was not detected. Include one only if it is relevant to the prompt, and describe it in your own terms.
essayIssues.too_short: This is a short draft ({words} words). Check the prompt's required length and add relevant, verified detail only if needed.
essayIssues.abrupt_paragraph_flow: Some paragraph openings do not show a detectable link to the previous idea. Check the progression; not every paragraph needs a transition word.
essayIssues.repeated_transition: The same transition appears repeatedly at paragraph openings. Vary it only where that makes the connection clearer.
essayIssues.action_verb_balance: The text check found more broad or weaker phrases than specific action verbs. Name what you did when accurate; keep softer wording when it is more truthful.
essayIssues.prompt_coverage_missing: {element} was not detected in the draft. Check the exact prompt; this text check may miss a valid response.

advice.relationshipMissing: Before sharing the brief, identify the recommender's role, how long they have known your work, and the class, project, or setting in which they observed you. This context lets an admissions reader judge how closely the writer can evaluate your abilities.
advice.relationshipProvided: You supplied this relationship note: “{relationship}”. Confirm the role, dates, and setting with the recommender, then let them rewrite it in their own voice. Remove any detail they did not observe or cannot verify.
advice.focusMissing: Review the target programme’s prompt, then identify qualities this recommender has personally observed and can support. Prepare a relevant example for each point if available; there is no universal number.
advice.focusMissingNoMajor: After identifying your actual target programme, review its prompt and note qualities the recommender has personally observed and can support. Use relevant examples where available; no universal number applies.
advice.focusProvided: You asked the recommender to consider “{focus}”. Keep this as a request, not a fact. Ask them to support each point with an example they personally observed, and make clear that they may revise or omit it.
advice.exampleMissing: Identify a concrete example from a class, project, research activity, team or service commitment that the recommender observed or can verify. Note the situation, your contribution and a verifiable result; include it only if relevant to the request.
advice.exampleProvided: You suggested “{example}”. Check names, dates, setting, your exact contribution, and the outcome. The recommender should use the example only if they directly observed it or can independently verify it, and should describe it in their own words.
advice.targetMajorMissing: Your profile does not identify an intended major or program. Add the exact field before sharing the brief so the recommender can explain why your evidence is relevant; do not ask them to guess your academic direction.
advice.evidencePresent: The profile contains {count} achievement, project or activity entries. Select examples based on the letter’s prompt, your direct knowledge and the space available; there is no fixed number. Prepare the context and a verifiable result for each example you choose.
advice.evidenceMissing: No project, award or activity details are recorded in the profile. Add accurate information if you have relevant examples, or discuss any work the recommender can verify. Do not invent a role, result or story.
advice.academicContext: Academic figures appear as profile context. Verify the GPA scale and test results against official records; the recommender should mention only what is relevant and must not imply they personally assessed an exam they did not supervise.

growthSeed.g3s4: Record only the result you actually achieve

growthSeed.g4s1: Set milestones that work for your schedule
growthSeed.g4s2: Keep dated notes or files showing your contribution

growthSeed.g5s1: Prepare a short introduction in your own words
growthSeed.g5s2: Practise with a trusted listener if useful
growthSeed.g5s3: Review specific feedback and decide what to refine

growthSeed.g6s3: Share the official prompt, submission method and deadline

growthSeed.p2h: What you cannot get at home and what you will bring back.

growthSeed.c2d: Follow each provider’s instructions and stated dates; do not assume that you must decline other offers.

growthSeed.c5t: Check whether an interview is required
growthSeed.c5d: If official guidance requires one, use it to prepare truthful answers; do not assume every destination requires an interview.
growthSeed.c6d: Evidence type, amount, account rules and coverage vary. Use the official destination checklist; do not assume a blocked account applies.
growthSeed.c7t: Plan how to access money after arrival
growthSeed.c7d: Review payment and banking options, fees and university guidance based on your needs; no specific card is required.
growthSeed.c8d: Availability, costs, eligibility and application dates differ. Confirm details with the university or official housing provider.
growthSeed.c9d: Confirm travel permission, programme dates and university arrival instructions before booking.
growthSeed.c10d: Rules vary by destination and programme. Verify official guidance before choosing or purchasing coverage.
growthSeed.c11d: Use the official checklist to decide which documents and copies to carry or store securely; protect personal information.
growthSeed.c12d: Confirm whether local or university registration applies, where to complete it and by when using official guidance.
growthSeed.g4s4: Share it only in formats accepted by the programme
growthSeed.g6s4: Confirm availability and track submission status
growthSeed.g7s4: Describe verified learning or outcomes without overstatement
growthSeed.c13d: Explore a SIM card, banking or transport options if useful; availability, fees and rules vary.
growthSeed.g8t: Prepare your academic transcript and grading scale legend
growthSeed.g8d: International universities evaluate your grades in the context of your official grading scale (5.0, 100-point or 4.0) and any required apostille or credential evaluation.
growthSeed.g8s0: Request an official transcript and grading scale legend from your school or university
growthSeed.g8s1: Verify whether target countries require a Hague Apostille (e.g. via my.gov.uz) or WES evaluation
growthSeed.g8s2: Arrange certified English or destination-language translations where required
growthSeed.g8s3: Check that course names, credit hours and graduation dates match across all documents
growthSeed.g9t: Draft a Master’s or scholarship research pre-proposal
growthSeed.g9d: Scholarships such as DAAD, MEXT, ETH ESOP and GKS Graduate require a structured study plan or research proposal aligned with host faculty.
growthSeed.g9s0: Identify a specific research question or applied problem in your field
growthSeed.g9s1: Review recent publications from 2–3 potential host laboratories or departments
growthSeed.g9s2: Outline your methodology, datasets and semester-by-semester study plan
growthSeed.g9s3: Have a professor or mentor review the draft for technical clarity and feasibility
growthSeed.g10t: Document community or civic impact with verifiable evidence
growthSeed.g10d: Scholarships like Chevening, Global UGRAD, Pearson and El-Yurt Umidi value sustained, verifiable contribution to your school or local community.
growthSeed.g10s0: Select an ongoing community, tutoring or civic initiative you actively support
growthSeed.g10s1: Keep a factual log of hours, dates, collaborators and concrete deliverables
growthSeed.g10s2: Gather a supervisor reference or official certificate confirming your role
growthSeed.g10s3: Connect what you learned to your post-graduation career plan
growthSeed.g11t: Build a multi-currency funding and scholarship portfolio
growthSeed.g11d: Combine institutional financial aid, bilateral government scholarships and national grants so your annual tuition and living costs are fully covered.
growthSeed.g11s0: Calculate total annual cost of attendance in the destination currency and USD
growthSeed.g11s1: Shortlist 3–5 scholarships whose eligibility, degree level and citizenship rules match your profile
growthSeed.g11s2: Prepare required financial documents (tax certificates, sponsor affidavit or CSS Profile)
growthSeed.g11s3: Track each scholarship deadline at least 6 weeks before the portal closes
growthSeed.p8q: Why did you choose this specific university and programme?
growthSeed.p8h: Name 2–3 concrete courses, professors or labs and link them to your prior preparation.

growthSeed.p9h: Name the specific sector, institution or reform where you will apply your skills in years 1–5.
growthSeed.p10q: Describe a time you built a network or partnership to solve a problem.
growthSeed.p10h: Essential for Chevening and GKS: show how you brought different people or groups together.
growthSeed.p11q: Explain any financial need or family circumstances relevant to your scholarship application.
growthSeed.p11h: State factual income, household dependents and confirmed family contribution clearly.
growthSeed.c14t: Complete Hague Apostille and certified translations
growthSeed.c14d: If your destination requires apostilled diplomas, transcripts or birth certificates (e.g. via my.gov.uz), complete them before your embassy appointment.
growthSeed.c15t: Prepare sponsor affidavit and income tax certificates
growthSeed.c15d: When parents or sponsors fund your studies, gather stamped bank statements, birth certificate relationship proof and official tax/income certificates.
growthSeed.c16t: Save dormitory or lease proof of address for visa filing
growthSeed.c16d: Many embassies require an official university dormitory placement letter or signed accommodation contract before issuing a study visa.
growthSeed.c17t: Activate student health insurance and municipal address registration
growthSeed.c17d: Complete mandatory post-arrival steps such as SEVIS check-in (US), Anmeldung & Girokonto activation (Germany), ARC (Korea) or BRP/eVisa check (UK).
growthSeed.c18t: Confirm the scholarship side of your offer
growthSeed.c18d: If the offer includes an award, confirm its conditions, renewal rules and reporting duties in writing with the provider before you accept.
growthSeed.c19d: Appointment waiting times vary by season and post. Check the official booking system for the current wait, then book rather than waiting for a perfect slot.
growthSeed.c20t: Set up a monthly budget for the first term
growthSeed.c20d: List rent, food, transport, insurance and one-off setup costs separately. The first term carries costs that later terms do not.
growthSeed.c21t: Read the tenancy terms before signing
growthSeed.c21d: Check deposit protection, notice period, whether utilities are included and who the contract is with. Never pay a deposit before seeing a contract.
growthSeed.c22t: Print and separately store key documents
growthSeed.c22d: Carry the passport, visa or permit decision, admission letter and insurance proof; keep digital copies somewhere you can reach without the originals.
growthSeed.c23t: Open a local bank account and phone line
growthSeed.c23d: Most destinations need a local address or registration number first, so sequence these after the registration step rather than before it.
growthSeed.c24t: Register with the student support office
growthSeed.c24d: Introduce yourself to the international student office in your first week: they handle the permits, extensions and institutional paperwork you will need later.

growthSeed.g12d: Prepare privately before opening application sections. Each platform and college asks different questions; enter only what the official form requests and never share sensitive family records unnecessarily.
growthSeed.g12s0: Check the current Common App or Apply with Scoir guide for the cycle you are using
growthSeed.g12s1: Privately gather likely parent or guardian details: legal name, contact, address, education, institutions and completion years, occupation, employer, and any other field the portal specifically asks
growthSeed.g12s2: Check whether country of birth or household-size questions apply to your account and cycle
growthSeed.g12s3: Enter only the requested information in the official secure application
growthSeed.g12s4: Review spellings and answers against primary records before submission
growthSeed.g13t: Build a transcript-matched coursework and honors inventory
growthSeed.g13d: Use the exact school transcript and the target platform's current labels. Dual-credit and current-course rules differ by application; verify each screen and never invent a course status or award tier.
growthSeed.g13s0: Copy course titles and codes exactly from the official transcript
growthSeed.g13s1: Check how the current application labels first- and second-semester courses in progress or not yet started
growthSeed.g13s2: For dual-enrollment credit, follow the platform's instructions for both high-school coursework and college information

growthSeed.g13s4: Check each award's official title, level and grade/year against evidence
growthSeed.g14t: Prepare concise activity entries with verified scope
growthSeed.g14d: Build an inventory before entering the portal. Up to ten Common App activity slots are available in the current guide, but fewer meaningful entries are fine; report actual hours, weeks, years and outcomes.
growthSeed.g14s0: List activities, responsibilities, work, hobbies and service that genuinely matter to you
growthSeed.g14s1: For each, verify role, organization, grade years, hours per week and weeks per year
growthSeed.g14s2: Draft an action-led description within the current portal character limit
growthSeed.g14s3: Use metrics only when you can support them and state your own contribution precisely
growthSeed.g14s4: Order entries by significance to your story rather than padding the list
growthSeed.p12q: What is an idea or subject you explored out of curiosity?
growthSeed.p12h: Show the question, what you did to investigate it, and how your understanding changed.
growthSeed.p13q: Describe a time you changed how you learned or contributed to a group.
growthSeed.p13h: Explain what you noticed, how you adapted, and what you learned from the people around you.
growthSeed.p14q: What small detail would help a future roommate get to know you?
growthSeed.p14h: Choose a concrete, human detail and let your own voice come through.
growthSeed.c25t: Prepare family information privately before opening the application
growthSeed.c25d: Use the current platform guide. You may want to locate a parent or guardian's legal name, email, address, phone, education and degrees, institutions and years, occupation/title, employer, and any birthplace or household-size fields only if the official form asks. Do not store or share sensitive family details in ScholarBridge.
growthSeed.c26t: Match coursework entries to the official transcript
growthSeed.c26d: Copy course codes and titles exactly from the transcript. Check the current portal's labels for first- and second-semester senior courses. For dual-enrollment credit, follow that platform's instructions for high-school coursework and college information; do not assume the same workflow across portals.
growthSeed.c27d: Common App's current first-year materials say applicants may report up to five academic honors. Prioritize by significance to your record; the International → National → State/Regional → School sequence is a planning heuristic, not an official admissions ranking. Confirm titles, years and recognition levels.
growthSeed.c28t: Draft a focused activity list with accurate time scope
growthSeed.c28d: Common App materials allow up to ten activities, but ten are not required. Track grades/years, actual hours per week and weeks per year in their designated fields; keep descriptions concise, action-led and evidence-based. Do not inflate scope or impact.
growthSeed.c29t: Prepare a recommender packet and ask early
growthSeed.c29d: Ask respectfully around a month or more before the earliest deadline where possible; this is a planning buffer, not a universal platform rule. Share a concise reflection/brag sheet and deadlines. Provide legal name, application ID, date of birth, high-school name and location only if the recommender or official portal needs them, using a secure channel rather than ordinary email.
growthSeed.c30t: Paste essays as plain text and check upload formats
growthSeed.c30d: Remove rich-text formatting before pasting into portal text boxes. Keep a clean text copy; export a PDF only when the college accepts or requests it. Check each portal's current file types, size limits and word/character counters—there is no universal PDF-only rule.
growthSeed.c31t: After submission, check each college's applicant portal
growthSeed.c31d: A submitted Common App or Apply with Scoir application may be followed by college-specific status instructions. Watch the email used on the application, open the official portal when invited, note any college-issued ID separately, and verify required scores, recommendations, portfolios and response dates. Invitation timing and decision deadlines vary; do not assume 24–72 hours or a universal May 1 date.

recommend.whyText: Only your fields of interest are required. Every other field is optional: adding it makes the match more precise, and skipping it never hurts you. Missing data is shown as “unknown” and is never counted against you.
recommend.prefilledNote: Prefilled from your saved profile. Edit or clear any field before running the match.

recommend.degreeLevelWhy: Optional — weighs programs at your level (Bachelor, Master, PhD…).
recommend.gpaWhy: Optional — compared with published program minimums. Enter the scale you use (4, 5, 100). Without a scale, a GPA above 4 is treated as unknown.
recommend.testsWhy: Optional — used only when a program publishes a minimum score.
recommend.countriesWhy: Optional — programs in these countries get a small ranking bonus. It never hides other countries.
recommend.budgetWhy: Optional — marks programs as within/over your budget. Tuition published in another currency is shown as unknown, never converted.
recommend.fundingWhy: Optional — need-based scholarship matches are shown only when you choose this.
recommend.languagePrefWhy: Optional — programs taught in this language rank slightly higher.
recommend.startYearWhy: Optional — used only to label the application cycle. It never filters results.

chancing.methodologyBody: Each answer above is computed separately. The match number is a weighted comparison with the preferences you saved; it never changes because of your grades, budget or a reported acceptance rate. Requirements are compared one by one and are never averaged into a score. The cost comparison never adds a bonus or a penalty to the match. Published statistics are compared with your recorded results only inside their published range, and no statistic is turned into a personal probability. A checklist is not a probability: no validated model for an individual admission probability is available, so none is shown.

software.trialTitle: Build a tiny calculator or to-do app
software.trialGoal: See whether turning instructions into working software feels satisfying.
software.trialStep1: Open any free beginner tutorial (for example the Python or JavaScript quick-start) and follow one lesson.
software.trialStep2: Change the program so it does something slightly different.
software.trialStep3: Write down what felt fun and what felt frustrating.
software.task1: Design and write code for apps and systems
software.task2: Debug problems and review teammates' code
software.task3: Meet with the team to plan features

data.trialTitle: Find one insight in a public dataset
data.trialGoal: Test whether turning raw numbers into a story excites you.
data.trialStep1: Download any free dataset (for example city weather or sports results) and open it in a spreadsheet.
data.trialStep2: Make one chart and describe in a sentence what it shows.
data.trialStep3: Note which part you enjoyed — cleaning, charting, or explaining.
data.task2: Build reports and dashboards for decisions

business.trialTitle: Plan a small event or fundraiser
business.trialGoal: See whether organising people, money and time is your kind of challenge.
business.trialStep1: Pick a small goal (a class event, a charity bake sale) and write a one-page plan.
business.trialStep2: List the budget, the people involved and the deadline.
business.trialStep3: Reflect: did planning this feel energising or exhausting?

engineering.trialTitle: Design and build a small structure
engineering.trialGoal: Find out whether designing physical things that must actually work suits you.
engineering.trialStep1: Build a bridge from paper or sticks that must hold a small weight.
engineering.trialStep2: Sketch your design first and note why each part is there.
engineering.trialStep3: Improve it once after testing — engineers iterate.
engineering.task3: Coordinate with suppliers and site teams

health.trialTitle: Follow a health science lesson and explain it
health.trialGoal: Check whether the science of the human body and caring for people appeals to you.
health.trialStep1: Watch one free anatomy or public-health lesson and take notes.
health.trialStep2: Explain what you learned to a friend or family member.
health.trialStep3: Notice whether the memorising and the caring both appeal to you.
health.task1: Examine patients and reason about symptoms
health.task2: Read research and follow clinical guidelines
health.task3: Work long, careful shifts with real responsibility

law.trialTitle: Argue both sides of a case
law.trialGoal: Test whether building careful arguments and reading fine print suits you.
law.trialStep1: Pick a real dispute from the news and write the strongest argument for each side.
law.trialStep2: Find one source (a law, a rule, a report) that supports each side.
law.trialStep3: Reflect on which side you found yourself supporting and why.

design.trialTitle: Redesign something you use every day
design.trialGoal: See whether making things clearer and more beautiful drives you.
design.trialStep1: Pick an app, package or room you use and sketch a better version.
design.trialStep2: Explain what problem your design solves.
design.trialStep3: Ask one person for feedback and note their reaction.
design.task1: Sketch concepts and build visual designs
design.task2: Work with clients to refine briefs

humanities.trialGoal: Check whether explaining ideas and shaping understanding is your strength.
humanities.trialStep1: Choose a topic you love and plan a 10-minute mini-lesson.
humanities.trialStep2: Teach it to a friend, sibling or even a camera.
humanities.trialStep3: Write down what worked and what confused your listener.

environment.trialGoal: See whether investigating and protecting natural systems appeals to you.
environment.trialStep1: Pick one environmental issue in your area (waste, water, air, green space) and observe it.
environment.trialStep2: Write a short note: what is happening, who it affects, what data is missing.
environment.trialStep3: Suggest one realistic action and note who would need to do it.
environment.task1: Study ecosystems, climate data and pollution

agriculture.trialTitle: Grow one plant and record the data
agriculture.trialGoal: Test whether patient, living systems work suits you.
agriculture.trialPrereq: A pot on a windowsill is enough
agriculture.trialStep1: Plant one seed and record water, light and growth every two days.
agriculture.trialStep2: Compare with a second plant treated differently.
agriculture.trialStep3: Summarise what the data taught you in three sentences.
agriculture.task1: Manage crops, animals or food production
agriculture.task2: Run field trials and soil or lab tests

media.trialTitle: Publish one story in any format
media.trialGoal: Check whether finding and telling stories drives you.
media.trialPrereq: A phone camera or a text post is enough
media.trialStep1: Interview one person or research one local topic.
media.trialStep2: Tell the story as an article, video or thread.
media.trialStep3: Note what your audience reacted to most.
media.task2: Write, edit, shoot or produce content
media.task3: Work to deadlines with editors and audiences

psychology.trialGoal: Find out whether understanding people and supporting them suits you.
psychology.trialStep1: Listen to a friend's problem for ten minutes without giving advice.
psychology.trialStep2: Summarise back what you heard and check you got it right.
psychology.trialStep3: Reflect: did listening feel natural or draining?
psychology.task1: Assess and support clients or research groups
psychology.task2: Run interviews, tests and behaviour studies

math.trialTitle: Solve a puzzle set and explain your methods
math.trialGoal: Test whether abstract thinking and proofs bring you satisfaction.
math.trialPrereq: Any free puzzle or olympiad set
math.trialStep1: Solve five problems from any free maths puzzle set.
math.trialStep2: Write full solutions — not just answers.
math.trialStep3: Note which kinds of problems you wanted more of.
math.task2: Apply maths to finance, science or engineering

science.trialTitle: Repeat a classic experiment at home
science.trialGoal: Check whether curiosity-driven investigation is your style.
science.trialStep1: Choose a safe classic experiment and predict the result in writing.
science.trialStep2: Run it carefully and record everything.
science.trialStep3: Compare prediction and result — and explain any difference.
science.task2: Publish papers and present at conferences

logistics.trialTitle: Plan the delivery route for a small task
logistics.trialGoal: See whether optimising real-world flows of goods and time suits you.
logistics.trialPrereq: Pen, paper and a map app
logistics.trialStep1: Plan how to move five items from one place to another within one day.
logistics.trialStep2: Minimise cost or time and explain your trade-offs.
logistics.trialStep3: Note which decisions kept you most engaged.
logistics.task2: Optimise routes, costs and delivery times

energy.trialTitle: Audit the energy use of your home
energy.trialGoal: Test whether making power cleaner and more efficient appeals to you.
energy.trialStep1: List every energy user in your home and estimate its share.
energy.trialStep2: Propose three realistic savings and rank them.
energy.trialStep3: Research one renewable option and note one advantage and one limitation.
energy.task1: Design power plants, grids or renewable systems
energy.task2: Run efficiency studies and safety checks
energy.task3: Work with regulators and field teams

tourism.trialTitle: Design a one-day tour for a visitor
tourism.trialGoal: Check whether creating experiences and hosting people delights you.
tourism.trialStep1: Plan a one-day itinerary for a first-time visitor to your city.
tourism.trialStep2: Include food, transport, timing and one surprise.
tourism.trialStep3: Present it to someone and note their questions.
tourism.task1: Design trips, events and guest experiences
tourism.task2: Manage bookings, staff and service quality
tourism.task3: Solve guest problems with a smile

hook.label: Concrete problem hook
hook.why: It opens on one specific, checkable moment — a place, a date, a number — so the reader meets the applicant's question before the biography.

preparation.label: Academic preparation in context
preparation.why: Grades and scores count for more next to their context — scale, rank, coursework — which shows the reader the applicant is ready for the next level.

evidence.label: Quantified evidence & metrics
evidence.why: It shows what the applicant personally did and what changed, with figures a referee could confirm — readers trust measured results more than adjectives.

gap.label: Honest gap → why this degree
gap.why: Naming the limit of current skills turns the degree into a logical next step instead of a wish.

fit.label: Programme & lab fit
fit.why: Named courses, labs or faculty that answer the gap prove the applicant researched this programme — the paragraph could not be pasted into another application.

community.label: Community contribution
community.why: It shows the applicant gives back, with numbers proving the effort was sustained rather than symbolic.

impact.label: Post-graduation impact in Uzbekistan
impact.why: A concrete role, institution and timeline make the return plan credible — the committee can picture exactly what its investment will build.

reflection.label: Turning point & reflection
reflection.why: A personal statement needs a change in thinking, not only events; this paragraph shows what the applicant learned and how it changed their choices.

leadership.label: Leadership without formal authority
leadership.why: Influence earned by understanding other people's problems first — the behaviour leadership questions are designed to find.

networking.label: Networking for impact
networking.why: The network was built to solve a problem, participants and outcomes are counted, and the paragraph says how the scholarship network will be used.

studyPlan.label: Semester-by-semester study plan
studyPlan.why: A dated plan with courses, a lab and a thesis target shows the committee exactly how its investment turns into skills.

letterhead.label: Letterhead, date & addressee
letterhead.why: Official letterhead, a date and a named committee make the document verifiable and show it was written for this application.

relationship.label: Recommender's standing & relationship
relationship.why: Praise can be weighed only when the reader knows how well, for how long and in what role the writer knows the applicant — and how the applicant compares with peers.

anecdote.label: Specific anecdote
anecdote.why: A story only this recommender could tell persuades far more than a list of adjectives.

character.label: Character & impact on others
character.why: It moves beyond grades to how the applicant treats and lifts other people, backed by concrete outcomes.

endorsement.label: Clear closing endorsement
endorsement.why: An unambiguous final recommendation — ideally with a ranking or “highest enthusiasm” — leaves no doubt about the writer's view.

signature.label: Signature & verifiable contact
signature.why: Full name, title, institution and an e-mail address let the committee confirm the letter is genuine.

heading.label: Clear title or subject line
heading.why: A precise title or subject tells the reader what the document is and what is being asked before they read further.

ask.label: One clear, easy request
ask.why: The request is specific, time-bound and easy to say yes to, with materials attached so the reader never has to search.

cvHeader.label: Header & positioning line
cvHeader.why: Name, contact details and a one-line positioning statement tell the reader at a glance who the applicant is and what they are applying for.

cvEducation.label: Education with context
cvEducation.why: Degree, dates, GPA with its scale and rank, and relevant coursework let a reader compare applicants fairly across countries.

cvExperience.label: Experience as achievement bullets
cvExperience.why: Each bullet starts with an action verb and ends with a result, so the reader sees outcomes rather than duties.

cvProjects.label: Projects & competitions
cvProjects.why: Named projects with tools, users and placements prove the applicant delivers outside the classroom.

cvLeadership.label: Leadership & service
cvLeadership.why: Leadership is shown through numbers — people recruited, students taught, outcomes reached.

cvRecognition.label: Publications & awards
cvRecognition.why: Awards and papers with the year, the venue and the level of selection show external validation.

cvSkills.label: Skills & languages
cvSkills.why: Concrete tools and test-backed language levels are easy to verify and to match against programme requirements.

visaPurpose.label: Purpose of study
visaPurpose.why: The officer hears a specific field, a reason and a career link — an unclear study purpose is a common refusal ground.

visaChoice.label: Why this university and country
visaChoice.why: Naming programme features and comparing options shows a genuine student decision rather than a route to migration.

visaFunding.label: Funding with exact figures
visaFunding.why: Who pays, how much and which document proves it — matching the figures on the admission documents.

visaTies.label: Home ties
visaTies.why: Family, property, employment or a contract obligation give concrete reasons to return home.

visaReturn.label: Concrete return plan
visaReturn.why: A named role and employer after graduation show that the study plan ends in Uzbekistan.

docParties.label: Parties & purpose
docParties.why: Every person is identified by full name and document number and the purpose is stated, so the reader can match it to passports and admission letters.

docAmount.label: Exact financial commitment
docAmount.why: Amounts in figures and in words, per year and for the whole programme, leave no room for ambiguity.

docEvidence.label: Evidence listed
docEvidence.why: Each claim points to an attached document, so the reader can verify instead of trusting.

docBudget.label: Budget & study plan
docBudget.why: Costs and funding add up line by line, and the plan connects the programme to a career.

docSignature.label: Declaration, signature & certification
docSignature.why: A truthfulness declaration, signature, date and notary certification make the document formally valid where it is required.

answer.label: Direct answer with evidence
answer.why: It answers the question in the first sentence and backs it with names and numbers within the word limit.

activity.label: Activity header
activity.why: Title, role, organisation and hours give the reader scale and commitment at a glance.

apostille.matrixTitle: What {country} asks for, document by document

uk_28_day.summary: UK Student Route: unpaid first-year tuition plus nine months of living costs, held for 28 consecutive days, with the closing balance dated no more than 31 days before the online application.

blocked_account.summary: Germany: a blocked account (Sperrkonto) with the published annual amount, or a blocking confirmation from a recognised provider such as Expatrio or Fintiba.

balance_certificate.summary: South Korea (D-2): a bank balance certificate for the published amount, issued for the visa application through the KVAC or the embassy.

gic_or_liquid.summary: Canada: the IRCC living-cost figure plus tuition and travel, held in liquid funds. A Guaranteed Investment Certificate (GIC) from a participating Canadian bank is accepted.

i20_amount.summary: United States (F-1): there is no national figure. The amount is set by your own Form I-20, issued by the school; the MRV fee and the SEVIS fee are separate.

liquid_available.summary: No visa minimum is published for this destination, so the figure shown is our annual living-cost benchmark for it — a planning floor, not an official requirement.

matrixNotes.united_kingdom: The UK does not require an apostille on academic documents for the Student Route, but UKVI does require a certified translation of anything not in English, and the financial evidence is where applications fail.
matrixNotes.united_states: US schools set their own document rules: many accept a certified translation without an apostille, while some require an apostilled diploma for credential evaluation (WES, ECE). Ask the graduate school in writing.
matrixNotes.germany: German universities and uni-assist generally require an apostille plus a sworn translation into German or English. Order the apostille on the ORIGINAL diploma before any copy is certified.
matrixNotes.south_korea: Korean universities and the visa office accept apostilled documents with a certified translation; the balance certificate is issued by your bank specifically for the visa file.
matrixNotes.canada: Canada joined the Apostille Convention in January 2024, so a Uzbek e-Apostille is now accepted in place of consular legalisation for most documents.
matrixNotes.italy: Italy requires an apostille plus a certified Italian translation, and a Declaration of Value (or CIMEA) for the diploma — start this before the pre-enrolment on Universitaly closes.
matrixNotes.hungary: Hungary accepts apostilled documents with a certified translation; several universities additionally ask for the original at enrolment, so keep the apostilled set unbound.

raise_gpa.title: Close the GPA gap to {target}
raise_gpa.why: Your admitted twin was selected with a GPA of {theirs}; yours is {mine}. GPA is the one row an admissions committee reads first and the hardest to change late.
raise_gpa.step1: List every remaining course and the grade each one needs to move your cumulative GPA to {target}.
raise_gpa.step2: Book the retake or the supplementary exam with your registry office this month, not next semester.
raise_gpa.step3: Record the new GPA and its scale on your profile so every match recalculates.

raise_english.title: Reach {target} on your English test
raise_english.why: Your twin held {theirs}; you have {mine}. A band short of the published minimum is the most common single reason an otherwise strong file is filtered out.
raise_english.step1: Book a sitting at least 60 days before your earliest deadline so a retake is still possible.
raise_english.step2: Work the weakest sub-score first — that is where one band is cheapest to gain.
raise_english.step3: Record the new score on your profile the day the result arrives.

add_standardized.title: Add a standardized test score of {target}
add_standardized.why: Your twin held {target}; you have {current}. Where a programme publishes a minimum, a missing score reads as an unfinished file.
add_standardized.step1: Check whether your target programmes actually require this test — many waived it permanently.
add_standardized.step2: Book a date that leaves room for one retake before your earliest deadline.
add_standardized.step3: Add the score to your profile so the requirement checks can see it.

add_research.title: Record {target} research outputs
add_research.why: Your twin had {theirs}; you have {mine}. For research programmes this is the row that separates a candidate who can start work from one who must be taught first.
add_research.step1: Ask one supervisor whether any existing project of yours can be written up or presented this term.
add_research.step2: Enter every output you already have — a conference poster and a preprint both count.
add_research.step3: Keep the DOI, link or acceptance email next to each entry so it can be verified.

add_activity_evidence.title: Record evidence in {target} activity fields
add_activity_evidence.why: Your twin had activity recorded in {theirs} fields; you have {mine}. An empty activity section makes a strong academic record look untested outside the classroom.
add_activity_evidence.step1: Fill in the fields you already have evidence for: projects, volunteering, olympiads, awards, clubs, sport.
add_activity_evidence.step2: For each one write the outcome, not the description — a number, a rank or a result.
add_activity_evidence.step3: Add one new activity this term that produces a verifiable outcome.

target_scholarship.title: Apply for {name}
target_scholarship.why: Your twin was funded by {name}{amount}. The same award is open to a profile like yours, and it changes the budget row entirely.
target_scholarship.step1: Open the award's official page and write down its deadline and its document list.
target_scholarship.step2: Check the requirement pills in the Scholarship Hub for this award and fix anything not met.
target_scholarship.step3: Add it to your funding plan so the amount is counted in your budget.

align_major.title: Align your field with {theirs}
align_major.why: Your twin was admitted in {theirs}; your recorded field is {mine}. Programmes filter on field first, and a mismatched label hides you from matches you would actually pass.
align_major.step1: Read the entry requirements of three programmes in {theirs} and note which of your courses they accept.
align_major.step2: Set your target major on your profile to the label those programmes use.
align_major.step3: Re-run your matches and shortlist the programmes your record actually supports.

quick.errInvite: That is a private invite link (t.me/+…). It carries no channel id — forward one post from the channel to the bot, or enter the -100… ID.
quick.errNotChannel: That does not look like a channel address. Enter @channel_name, https://t.me/channel_name or the -100… ID.

quick.connectSaved: Channel saved, but the mode is Off — nothing will be posted.

env.panelHint: These values live in the hosting environment, not in this panel. The panel shows what is set and whether it is usable; change them in Render → Environment, then redeploy.

where.CHANNEL_AUTOPOST: Optional ceiling. Unset = this panel decides. off = hard kill switch. dryrun = live posting impossible (everything goes to the admin chat).
where.TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_ID: Your channel: @username or the −100… id (Telegram → channel → a post → Copy link → t.me/c/…).
where.TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID: Your own Telegram id: send /id to the bot in a private chat (or @userinfobot).
where.CHANNEL_SITE_URL: Your public site origin, e.g. https://example.org — used to build post links. Falls back to APP_URL.
where.APP_URL: The same site origin; already set on most deployments. Used when CHANNEL_SITE_URL is empty.
where.CHANNEL_DISCUSSION_ENABLED: 1 enables the “discuss in comments” call-to-action. Optional.
where.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: BotFather → /mybots → your bot → API Token. Optional here: the bot settings tab stores it encrypted.

env.envUnset: CHANNEL_AUTOPOST is not set — the panel controls posting
env.envKill: CHANNEL_AUTOPOST=off is set on the server and overrides the panel
env.envDryrun: CHANNEL_AUTOPOST=dryrun is set on the server (the panel can only make it quieter)
env.envOn: CHANNEL_AUTOPOST=on is set on the server (the panel decides)

why.title: Why is nothing being posted?
why.readyNext: All good — the next post is due today at {time}.
why.readyNoNext: All good — today's posts are out; the next one is planned tomorrow.
why.catalogueLine: Catalogue: {publishable} ready to publish (of {total}; {verified} verified, {exact} with an exact deadline).
why.thin: Thin catalogue: fewer than 10 publishable programmes, so the channel will start repeating itself.
why.cronTitle: The automatic tick is not running
why.cronBody: When the site is idle, the in-process timer sleeps with it. Add this URL to UptimeRobot (every 5 minutes): it keeps the site awake and drives the queue.
why.cronNoSecret: CRON_SECRET is not set — this URL answers 503. Add it to the hosting environment.
why.unpublishedTitle: In the catalogue but not publishable:
why.token_missing: No bot token. Add it in Admin → Telegram.
why.env_off: CHANNEL_AUTOPOST=off — posting is disabled on the server. Change it in the hosting settings.
why.mode_off: The mode is Off. Choose Approval or Live in the connect section.
why.paused: Paused until {date}. Clear the pause date to continue.
why.channel_missing: No channel set. Enter the @username or -100… id in the field above.
why.channel_unreachable: Channel «{channelId}» was not found. Check that the bot is an administrator in it.
why.channel_wrong_type: That id is not a channel ({type}). Enter the channel's @username or -100… id.
why.bot_not_admin: The bot is not an administrator. Channel → Administrators → add the bot and grant «Post messages».
why.no_post_permission: «Post messages» is switched off. Enable it in Channel → Administrators.
why.admin_chat_missing: No admin chat id — there is nowhere to approve a post. Open the bot in your own chat, send /start and enter the numeric id.
why.admin_chat_unreachable: The admin chat is unreachable. Open the bot in that chat once and send /start.
why.site_missing: No site URL — links in the posts will be dropped.
why.site_not_public: «{url}» is not an https address; Telegram will strip the links.
why.catalogue_empty: The catalogue is empty ({total}). Programmes are needed before anything can be posted.
why.catalogue_stale: There are {total} programmes but none publishable: {verified} verified, {stale} with a stale verification. Re-verify them in Admin → Programmes.
why.catalogue_no_deadlines: {publishable} publishable programmes, but none has an exact deadline — no «3 days left» reminders can be produced.
why.quiet_day: Today is a quiet day — a rest day by design. It can be turned off in the Plan section.
why.plan_empty: Today's plan came out empty. Press «Build today's plan».
why.waiting_for_time: Queued — the next post goes out at {time}.
why.cron_stale: The last automatic check was {minutes} min ago (it should run every {interval} min). Check the UptimeRobot URL.
why.startDone: Publishing is on — the first post arrived in the admin chat.

adminAccounts.loadFailed: Could not load the account list.
adminAccounts.failed: The action did not complete. Nothing was changed.
adminAccounts.yourPasswordHint: Required for every change on this screen
adminAccounts.linkBody: The student sets a new password themselves — you never see it. The link works once, for 60 minutes, and is not emailed: copy it and send it through Telegram or WhatsApp. This is the option that works even when email delivery is down.
adminAccounts.linkReady: Reset link created. Send it to the student now:
adminAccounts.linkExpiry: Valid until {when}. Creating another link cancels this one.
adminAccounts.passwordBody: Only if the student cannot open a link. The old password cannot be recovered — it can only be replaced. Every device signed in on this account is signed out immediately.
adminAccounts.passwordReady: Password changed for {email}. It is not emailed to anyone — give it to the student yourself.
adminAccounts.passwordShownOnce: Shown once. It is not stored anywhere in readable form, so copy it now if you need it.
adminAccounts.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it manually.
adminAccounts.whyNoPassword: No screen can show an account's password: it is stored as a one-way scrypt hash, so even the database has nothing to decode. What an administrator can do is what this page does — replace it with a new one, or issue a link the student uses to choose their own. Both are recorded in the audit log under the administrator's name.
adminAccounts.yourPasswordWhose: This is the password for {email} — last set {when}. It is YOURS, not the student's.
adminAccounts.viewerNoPasswordTitle: Your admin account has no password yet
adminAccounts.viewerNoPasswordBody: An account created through Telegram can have no password at all, so there is nothing to confirm with. Open Edit Profile and set one, then type it here.
adminAccounts.viewerLegacyTitle: This password cannot be verified by this build
adminAccounts.viewerLegacyBody: The stored value is in an older format that this version cannot check, so every attempt would look like a wrong password. Set a new password in Edit Profile and type that here.
adminAccounts.reauthMismatchTitle: That was not the password of this admin account
adminAccounts.reauthMismatchBody: The field wants the password you sign in with as {email} — not the student's, and not an old one. If you do not remember it, open Edit Profile, set a new one, and type that here.
adminAccounts.errInvalidPassword: That is not the password for {email}. This field asks for YOUR OWN password — not the student's.
adminAccounts.errPasswordNotSet: Your admin account has no password yet. Set one in Edit Profile first, then come back.
adminAccounts.errPasswordFormatLegacy: Your account's stored password is in an old format that cannot be checked. Set a new password in Edit Profile, then try again.
adminAccounts.errRateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
adminAccounts.errAppUrlMissing: The server has no APP_URL configured, so a full reset link cannot be built. Set APP_URL on the deployment and retry.
adminAccounts.errSelfTarget: You cannot reset your own password from here — use Edit Profile.
adminAccounts.errWeakPassword: That password does not meet the rules: at least 8 characters, and not an easily guessed one.
adminAccounts.errAmbiguousRequest: The request carried two passwords at once. Send either a typed password or "generate", not both.
adminAccounts.selfBody: Replace the password for {email} right here — no old password needed, because this signed-in session is the proof. Your other devices are signed out and you stay signed in on this one.
adminAccounts.selfBodyNoViewer: Replace the password you sign in with, right here. No old password needed — this session is the proof. Your other devices are signed out.
adminAccounts.selfPolicy: At least 8 characters, not an easily guessed one.
adminAccounts.selfDoneTitle: Your password is now this. It is already in the confirmation field above:
adminAccounts.selfDoneBody: Every other device was signed out. Write it down — the app cannot show it to you again, but you can always replace it from this card.
adminAccounts.selfErrWeak: That password does not meet the rules: at least 8 characters, and not an easily guessed one.
adminAccounts.selfErrMismatch: The two passwords do not match.

adminRefresh.title: Data Refresh Center
adminRefresh.subtitle: Two distinct modes. Scheduled runs come from the cron endpoint.
adminRefresh.statusModeHint: Recompute application/verification state from dates already stored. Never re-reads an official page and never changes verified dates.
adminRefresh.officialModeHint: Actually re-reads the official page, verifies one specific fact and only then may refresh a verified date. A failed check leaves the date untouched.
adminRefresh.noDatesMoved: No verified dates were changed. An HTTP 200 alone is not verification; a specific source-backed fact is required.

adminReviewQueue.title: Evidence Review Queue
adminReviewQueue.subtitle: Source-less facts, stale checks, conflicts and failed jobs — with a reason and a next step.
adminReviewQueue.migrationPending: The review queue migration is not applied yet.
adminReviewQueue.reasonRequired: A written reason is required for every decision.
adminReviewQueue.neverAutoVerified: Opening or deciding an item never marks a fact verified; a separate official-source check is required.

factEditor.title: Scoped catalogue facts (advanced)
factEditor.hint: Use original values and exact programme, cycle, applicant scope and units. Groups use allOf / anyOf / not_applicable. Every edit returns to review-needed; a JSON verification flag is not proof. A conflicting version preserves your draft.
factEditor.saved: Saved as review-needed. Verify the exact field against its official source.
factEditor.reviewHint: Only for requirement_group: manually read the publisher page. This attests the exact saved version, scope, AND/OR relationships and every leaf; it does not claim a network reread. Edits must be saved first.
factEditor.quote: Quote from the official source (at least 40 characters)
factEditor.attest: I checked this exact saved group, all alternatives, sections, dates and scope against the official source.
factEditor.reviewed: Manual source review recorded; no automated page reread was claimed.
